subject: geography
intro: Geography leads to paid work measuring and managing the Earth's surface — mapping it, surveying it, studying how people use it, and planning the cities and regions built on it.

roles.title: Cartographers and Photogrammetrists
roles.what: Research, study and prepare maps and other spatial data in digital or graphic form for legal, social, political, educational and design purposes, often working with geographic information systems and imagery.
roles.where: The syllabus's map-and-diagram reading across river, coastal and tectonic units — drainage basins, landforms, plate boundaries — builds the spatial fluency of representing terrain that cartography professionalises.

roles.title: Geographers
roles.what: Study the nature and use of areas of the Earth's surface, relating and interpreting interactions between physical and cultural phenomena — from landforms and climate to the human patterns laid over them.
roles.where: This is the syllabus as a career: physical units on rivers, coasts, ecosystems and climate change meet human units on population, migration and urbanisation in exactly the combined way geographers practise.

roles.title: Surveying and Mapping Technicians
roles.what: Perform surveying and mapping duties under the direction of surveyors, cartographers or engineers — taking the field measurements that fix boundaries, guide construction and feed mapmaking.
roles.where: Fieldwork across the syllabus — measuring river and coastal processes, observing urban change — rehearses the observation-and-recording discipline technicians perform with instruments in the field.

roles.title: Urban and Regional Planners
roles.what: Develop comprehensive plans and programmes for how land and physical facilities are used across towns, cities, counties and metropolitan areas, weighing growth against environmental and community needs.
roles.where: The changing-towns-and-cities unit — where people live, urbanisation's opportunities and challenges — plus hazards and climate-change units are the working brief of planners deciding what gets built where.
